main_strengths: Consistent Keynesian vocabulary and mechanisms: effective demand, multiplier, output gap, sticky wages/prices, liquidity preference, counter-cyclical fiscal policy
Historical analogs are mostly real and pre-2025 (Iran-Iraq 1988, Dayton 1995, Colombia 2016, NotPetya 2017, demonetisation 2016, 2011 IEA release); no invented institution-attributed statistics

Some trajectories respond well to the event's sign: peace deal (k0004) and RBA QE (k0007) go risk-on; blockade (k0005) and party exit (k0012) get oil LONG; inflation expectations (k0019) handles stagflation with bonds NEUTRAL
Tool-use structure (Think -> episode DB -> Think -> macro data -> Think -> Output) is followed in all 19
main_problems: Fixed demand-shortfall prior: every trajectory concludes 'demand shortfall, not overheating', even with 3.4-4.0% unemployment and 4-6% inflation (k0002, k0007, k0014, k0017); a Keynesian output-gap reading should flip to overheating or supply constraint there

Keyword stuffing: paradox of thrift, animal spirits, liquidity trap and multiplier appear in nearly every chain whether relevant or not (3-day outage, peace deal, CPI print); the student will learn a checklist, not a theory

Signal defaults: equities SHORT 15/19, gold LONG 18/19, bonds LONG 18/19, oil SHORT 15/19, USD NEUTRAL (conv 2) 12/19. Gold LONG is argued in about 3 cases; equities SHORT is unjustified for the SPR release (k0001) and the 3-day LatAm outage (k0009), and overconfident for single-EM shocks (k0008)
Scenario probabilities templated: 0.45/0.30/0.15/0.10 in 9/19, S4=0.10 in 15/19; scenarios are labels with no direction, horizon or mapping to signals
Snapshot leakage: in 16/19 the first Think already quotes snapshot values before get_macro_data is called, which makes the tool call pointless and teaches incoherent tool use
Snapshot/event contradictions not caught (k0006 'deepest inversion' vs +38bp 2s10s; k0008 curve statement); synthetic snapshots often internally implausible
Supply shocks (solar storm, pandemic, drought, SPR) forced into a pure aggregate-demand frame; stagflation trade-off rarely analysed
Non-US events (RBA, BoE, LatAm, EM) mapped to US-centric assets with no FX/spillover reasoning; one wrong-signed USD call (k0017)

Analogs are often vague era labels ('2008-09 banking-stress episode', '2011-2012 soft-inflation episode') with Keynesian-flavoured embellishments (e.g., fiscal transfers in 2018-19); some mischaracterisations (2015-16 oil as geopolitical, 1989 Quebec 'prolonged', 2007-08 inversion)
Tool-call argument formats and indicator names vary randomly (JSON, bare text, 'query:', 'request:', typos like 'qqq')
suggested_prompt_or_template_changes: Require an explicit output-gap sign check from the snapshot (unemployment vs a stated NAIRU, inflation vs target) before diagnosing; allow and expect 'positive gap / overheating' and 'supply-constrained' conclusions

Require one justification sentence per asset signal tied to a causal-chain step; permit NEUTRAL and demand it when the event is small or local; add a balance check across the pilot that rejects batches where any asset's direction exceeds about 70%
Stop listing Keynesian keywords in the teacher prompt as must-use; instead ask for the one or two mechanisms most relevant to this event, and reject outputs that use more than N school buzzwords
Do not show the macro snapshot to the teacher before the get_macro_data Observe, or post-filter trajectories whose pre-tool Think quotes snapshot numbers

Make scenarios structured: each with direction for growth/inflation, horizon, and probability not drawn from a fixed template; reject the 0.45/0.30/0.15/0.10 pattern and require signals to follow the probability-weighted scenarios

Have the episode DB return real retrieved analogs (with dates/country) rather than letting the teacher write them; or require named, dated, country-specific episodes and auto-check against a whitelist
Add an event-sign and event-scale field (positive/negative, local/global) to templates and check signals against it; for non-US events require FX and spillover reasoning
Validate synthetic snapshots for internal consistency (curve vs event text, mortgage vs 10y, VIX vs GDP) or instruct the teacher to flag contradictions explicitly
Normalise tool-call argument schema (always JSON with fixed indicator keys) in post-processing
Fix template wording errors (BoE 'chair' -> Governor) and ask the teacher to treat supply shocks as supply shocks with demand second-round effects
